text:
incbot: :rotating_light: paging @oncall-sre @netops @runtime — p99 tail latency spike detected for streaming responses in eu-west-2 (service: inference-stream). p99 2.4s (SLO 250ms), p95 1.1s. Errors: streaming stalls / stalled chunks. Alert ID: A-2026-7890

jordan: I’m on it. grabbing dashboard links and customer impact. what’s the window on the page?

sam: seeing a correlated spike in TLS handshake retries and inter-AZ retransmits out of eu-west-2b -> nat-gw. net metrics show increase in SYN retransmits and 5xx on edge. suspect cross-zone path flaps + NAT ephemeral port pressure.

lee: confirming streaming stalls map to long tail handshakes. traces show many streams stuck waiting on TLS handshake for >1s before application starts to send tokens.

mira: runtime note — when TCP stalls >700ms our streaming spin loop adds backpressure and kv-cache flushes more frequently; this amplifies tail. we saw request concurrency backlog increase ~3x.

carter: support: 3 paying customers reported slow/open streams (IDs: C-5521, C-6633, C-7742). One customer noticed timeouts on long polls. prioritizing SLAs.

jordan: runbook ref: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress-nat-issue> — follow egress-handoff section. immediate plan: 1) quick mitigation: steer egress for critical fleets to standby nat pool in region, 2) reduce per-connection streaming chunk size and enable early-send to avoid head-of-line, 3) enable temporary fallback routing to eu-west-1 for non-PII traffic.

sam: initiating egress steer to standby pool for fleet: infra-fleet-eu-stream-1. command (internal admin API):

```
POST https://admin.internal/egress/steer
{
  "fleet": "infra-fleet-eu-stream-1",
  "target_pool": "eu-west-2-standby-nat",
  "reason": "urgent p99 tail nat noise",
  "ttl": 900
}
```

sam: response: 202 accepted. starting drain on old pool. monitoring conntrack counts and ephemeral ports.

lee: i'm patching a conntrack-tuning change on the worker hostgroup (short-term): reducing conntrack timeout for TIME_WAIT-ish flows and enabling net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1 to help reclaim ephemeral ports quickly. running via chef scale group.

mira: pushing runtime flag: streaming.chunk_size=256 -> 512 fallback to reduce small-packet penalty. pushing to canary 5% now. command: `redwoodctl rollout set-config runtime/streaming chunk_size=256 --canary=5`

ops-bot: deploy started: rollout id r-2026-998. canary 5% -> success. monitoring metrics.

jordan: keeping customers informed. carter — please update the two customers in the next 15m with the mitigation steps and expected recovery window.

carter: Will do. pinging them now, noting mitigation and ask for any logs.

sam: after steer, TLS handshake retries dropped ~60% within 45s. SYN retransmits decreased. p99 dropped from 2.4s -> 980ms. still above SLO but much better.

lee: further lowered connection throttles on proxy level, and disabled aggressive muxing for streaming for the canary group to avoid head-of-line from a single bad TCP.

mira: runtime canary shows p99 for canary group at 420ms. global p99 trending down to ~700ms.

jordan: good. next steps: 1) hold current steer for 30m and observe, 2) if stable, expand canary to 50% and re-evaluate, 3) prepare for handoff to night oncall with full notes.

sam: noted. I’ll also raise a ticket with cloud provider — NAT gateway showed high ephemeral port exhaustion signals around 15:36 UTC, likely due to sudden increase in ephemeral reuse. Provider may provision additional ephemeral capacity or allow larger port allocation.

lee: action item: create a follow-up to audit: connection churn causes, client-side keepalive behavior, and whether we can enable client-side connection pooling guidance in SDK.

carter: customer update posted: "We’re seeing improved response times after network reroute; engineering is continuing mitigations and we’ll follow up with a postmortem." Customers acknowledged.

jordan: rolling to 50% runtime canary now. ops-bot started rollout r-2026-999.

ops-bot: rollout r-2026-999: canary 50% -> success.

sam: metrics check: global p95 160ms (within SLO), p99 ~320ms after 50% canary and egress steer; still higher than target because some legacy fleets still on old path. overall error rates down to baseline.

mira: I’ll keep runtime flags in place until we finish postmortem; will include toggle to revert quickly if regressions happen.

jordan: summarizing for handoff — Incident start 3987654321. Symptoms: p99 tail spike 2.4s from streaming stalls caused by inter-AZ TLS handshake noise and NAT ephemeral pressure. Mitigations: egress steer to standby NAT pool, conntrack tuning, runtime chunk-size canary, proxy mux adjustments. Result: p99 improved to ~320ms, p95 within SLO, customers reporting improvement.

jordan: assigning postmortem owner: lee. please include timeline, root cause hypothesis (cross-zone routing + NAT ephemeral exhaustion + client churn), RCA steps, and remediation (long term NAT capacity + connection pooling guidance + runtime backpressure improvements).

lee: ack, will author. target draft by EOD and final postmortem by tomorrow.

incbot: :white_check_mark: Incident A-2026-7890 marked "mitigated" at 3987654598. Please file postmortem and link runbook updates.

jordan: handing off to night oncall @oncall-night. handoff notes saved: https://redwood.internal/incidents/A-2026-7890/hand-off. If p99 rises >600ms or streaming error rate >1% re-escalate immediately. Good work all :thumbsup:

carter: closing customer comms for now; will reopen if they see regressions.

mira: leaving a runtime perf regression check for next week.

sam: filing cloud ticket and provider follow-up: CT-29872.

lee: creating postmortem doc and updating runbook with a new section: "nat-egress-handoff - provider signals and egress-steer play".

jordan: thanks team.
